neighbours.label: Warning against concluding from appearances: ' because' in 'Just because X doesn't mean Y', and ' by' in 'judge ... by'; causal 'because' and other uses of 'by' stay quiet.
fire: Just because the sky is grey doesn't mean it will rain.
Just because a dog barks does not mean it bites.
Don't judge a book by its cover.
Never judge a person by their clothes.
Visitors are often fooled by the plain front of the shop.
Just because he smiled doesn't mean he agreed.
You can't tell much by looking at the label.
And just because it's cheap doesn't mean it's bad.
quiet: It will rain because the sky is grey.
The dog barks because the mail has come.
Don't carry a book by its spine.
Never wash a sweater by machine.
Visitors are often driven by bus to the front of the shop.
You can't pay much by check at the store.

notes: The output direction promotes ' appearances', ' visible', ' appear'. Probes: 'Just because' 0.51, 'judge ... by' 0.64; causal 'because' 0.03-0.05. The two triggers share one meaning: it looks like X, but that doesn't settle it.
